justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain SubstanceNucleicAcid in base R6 as a deprecated transitional resource while introducing SubstanceDefinition.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve old instances, but would prolong duplicate substance models, endpoints, generated classes, and ambiguity about the preferred source of truth.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Consolidating the draft R4 IDMP-style substance resources into the broader `SubstanceDefinition` model is a reasonable inferred R6 goal, and a major-version ballot is a plausible place to remove obsolete core surface area. The break is still severe for adopters, but the main less-breaking base-design path would keep a deprecated resource beside its successor, which has material long-term interoperability and maintenance costs. Because no local change rationale or official conversion map was available, this is not assessed as fully justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking base R6 design would be to keep the concrete `SubstanceNucleicAcid` resource in core as deprecated for a transition period, with definitions and guidance pointing implementers toward `SubstanceDefinition`. Ordinary conversion tooling, profiles, or extension packages would be useful mitigations but are not counted as the base-design alternative. Keeping the old resource would preserve `resourceType` and old paths, but it risks an indefinite legacy model and duplicate representations of the same substance definition.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Carry the R4 nucleic-acid subunit/linkage/sugar model forward as optional base R6 content, either on a deprecated SubstanceNucleicAcid resource or as structured optional content in SubstanceDefinition.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Structured preservation would reduce data loss, but would make the generic substance model larger and create competing generic versus specialized encodings.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A generic `SubstanceDefinition.structure.representation` model is a reasonable simplification goal, but the local evidence does not show why R6 needed to drop all standardized structured nucleic-acid detail from the base design. The data at risk can be scientifically and regulatorily material, and the report's extension/profile/conversion-map options are mitigations rather than backwards-compatible base designs. A base alternative exists, but it has substantial duplication and complexity costs, so the availability is only partial.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base-design alternative would preserve the old structured facts as optional R6 content: for example, keep `SubstanceNucleicAcid` deprecated with its subunit/linkage/sugar paths, or add governed optional nucleic-acid structure backbones to `SubstanceDefinition`. That could preserve most R4 data while allowing generic representations for simpler cases. The tradeoff is material validation ambiguity: the same sequence, linkage, or sugar facts could appear in both generic representations and specialized fields, and deprecated representations may never fully disappear.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Avoid the codegen break only by retaining a deprecated core resource definition that R6 generators can still emit.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would prevent enum/class/endpoint failures, but would keep legacy generated API surface and duplicate runtime paths in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The runtime and code-generation break follows directly from accepting the core artifact removal. If R6's goal was to consolidate substance modeling and remove obsolete draft resource surface area, then dropping the generated class and REST type is probably justified. Compatibility SDKs or generated aliases are valuable migration mitigations, but they are not less-breaking base R6 designs unless the core package keeps a resource definition to generate from.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base-design alternative would be to leave a deprecated `SubstanceNucleicAcid` StructureDefinition in R6 so generated validators, model libraries, resource-type enums, and REST dispatch tables still include it while warning implementers to migrate. A non-core cross-version library or converter would not count as the base alternative here. The cost is maintaining stale generated surface area and two runtime routes for substance-definition content.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain conditional nucleic-acid interpretation rules in base R6 SubstanceDefinition structure/representation definitions.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This has low structural cost, but adds subtype-specific guidance to a generic resource and may not cover every regulated migration case.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving to a generic substance-definition resource is reasonable, but losing the old 5-prime-to-3-prime, default subunit count, subunit ordering, and linkage-default semantics appears avoidable. Unlike preserving every old element, retaining these assumptions as conditional base conformance text or representation-format guidance would not substantially duplicate the data model. The supplied evidence does not show why R6 needed to omit that interpretive bridge.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would add conditional text to `SubstanceDefinition.structure` or `SubstanceDefinition.structure.representation` stating how nucleic-acid sequence representations should be interpreted, including sequence direction, omitted subunit count, subunit ordering, and default linkage connectivity. A profile or conversion guide would also help implementers, but the counted alternative is the low-cost base R6 text/guidance itself.
